<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Satellite network includes costs of the constellation of satellites, and the ground and control facilities, consisting of GESs, gateway control centers and the network control center.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2019 and 2018, assets under construction primarily consist of costs associated with acquiring, developing, enhancing and testing software and hardware for internal and external use that have not yet been placed into service. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000459" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000459_cnt_1">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Valuation of long-lived assets</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Property and equipment and other long-lived assets are tested for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that their carrying amounts may not be recoverable. The Company measures recoverability by comparing the carrying amounts of the assets to the projected undiscounted cash flows the assets are expected to generate. An impairment loss is recognized to the extent the carrying values exceed the fair values.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s satellite constellation and related assets are evaluated as a single asset group whenever facts or circumstances indicate that the carrying values may not be recoverable. If indicators of impairment are identified, recoverability of long-lived assets is measured by comparing their carrying amounts to the projected cash flows the assets are expected to generate.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Determining whether an impairment has occurred typically requires the use of significant estimates and assumptions, including the allocation of cash flows to assets or asset groups and, if required, estimates of fair values for those assets or asset groups.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">If a satellite were to fail while in orbit, the resulting loss would be charged to expense in the period it is determined that the satellite is not recoverable. The amount of any such loss would be reduced to the extent of insurance proceeds, if any, estimated to be received. During the year ended December 31, 2017, an impairment loss of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000593" name="orbc:ImpairmentChargeSatelliteNetwork" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_orbcOrbcommGenerationTwoSatelliteMember_20170101_20171231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">31,224</ix:nonFraction> was recorded to write off the net book value relating to the Company&#8217;s in-orbit OG2 satellites. There was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000594" name="us-gaap:GainLossOnSalesOfAssetsAndAssetImpairmentCharges" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_orbcSatelliteNetworkMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000595" name="us-gaap:GainLossOnSalesOfAssetsAndAssetImpairmentCharges" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_orbcSatelliteNetworkMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> impairment loss recorded for the years ended December 31, 2019 and 2018. See &#8220;Note 6 &#8211; Satellite Network and Other Equipment, Net&#8221; for additional details relating to the impairment of these satellites. </p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-15</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000424_dcnt_47a7bb73-675b-4d6c-924d-a08a5e8efd1b" continuedAt="F_000424_dcnt_6b7d37f8-896f-4591-8eec-db209476ae01"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000460" name="us-gaap:ResearchDevelopmentAndComputerSoftwarePolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capitalized development costs for internal and external use </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company capitalizes the costs of acquiring, developing and testing software and hardware to meet the Company&#8217;s internal needs and for products and services that have not yet been placed into service. Capitalization of costs associated with software obtained or developed for internal use commences when both the preliminary project stage is completed and management has authorized further funding for the project, based on a determination that it is probable that the project will be completed and used to perform the function intended. Capitalized costs include only (1)&#160;the external direct cost of materials and services consumed in developing or obtaining internal-use software, (2)&#160;payroll and payroll-related costs for employees who are directly associated with, and devote time to, a qualifying project, and (3) certain external software development costs upon the establishment of technological feasibility. Technological feasibility is considered to have occurred upon completion of either a detailed program design or a working model. Capitalization of such costs ceases no later than the point at which the project is substantially complete and ready for its intended use. Internal-use software costs are amortized once the software is placed in service using the straight-line method over periods ranging from <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000596" name="orbc:CapitalizedSoftwareDevelopmentAmortizationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001361983_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" continuedAt="C_8b929fa0-f06a-454a-95d3-477f13634762">three</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000597" name="orbc:CapitalizedSoftwareDevelopmentAmortizationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001361983_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">seven<ix:continuation id="C_8b929fa0-f06a-454a-95d3-477f13634762"> years</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>. Product and service development costs are amortized over the estimated life of the product once it has been released for commercial sale.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000461" name="orbc:CapitalizedPatentDefenseCostsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capitalized patent defense costs </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company capitalizes costs incurred in connection with the defense of a patent the Company owns when the defense against the alleged infringer is deemed probable of success, and the costs will increase the value of the patent. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000462" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsGoodwillPolicy" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill represents the excess of the purchase price over the underlying net tangible and intangible assets of the Company&#8217;s acquisitions. Goodwill is not amortized, but is tested for impairment on an annual basis and between annual tests whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount may not be recoverable. Goodwill is tested at the reporting unit level, which is defined as an operating segment or one level below the operating segment. The Company operates in <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_orbcSegment" id="F_000598" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> reportable segment which is its only reporting unit. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company tests for an indication of goodwill impairment annually on November&#160;30 or when an indicator of impairment exists, by comparing the fair value of the reporting unit to its carrying value. If there is an indication of impairment, the Company performs a &#8220;step two&#8221; test to measure the impairment. There was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000599" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000600" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" contextRef="C_0001361983_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000601" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" contextRef="C_0001361983_20170101_20171231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> impairment of goodwill for the years ended December&#160;31, 2019, 2018 and 2017. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000463" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsIntangibleAssetsPolicy" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Intangible assets </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Intangible assets that are not considered to have an indefinite life are amortized over their useful lives. Intangible assets include patents and technology, customer lists and trademarks. Intangible assets are amortized using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:continuation id="F_000459_cnt_1">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Impairment of long-lived assets </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company reviews its long-lived assets and amortizable intangible assets whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable. In connection with this review, the Company also re-evaluates the periods of depreciation and amortization for these assets. The Company recognizes an impairment loss when the sum of the future undiscounted net cash flows expected to be realized from the asset is less than its carrying amount. If an asset is considered to be impaired, the impairment to be recognized is measured by the amount by which the carrying amount of the asset exceeds its fair value, which is determined using the projected discounted future net cash flows, using the appropriate discount rate. </p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000465" name="us-gaap:StandardProductWarrantyPolicy" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Warranty costs </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company accrues for warranty coverage on product sales estimated at the time of sale based on historical costs to repair or replace products for customers compared to historical product sales. The warranty accrual is included in accrued liabilities on the Company&#8217;s consolidated balance sheets. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Separately-priced extended warranty coverage is recorded as warranty revenue over the term of the extended warranty coverage and the related warranty costs are recorded as incurred during the coverage period. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Warranty coverage that includes additional services, such as repairs and maintenance of the product, is treated as a separate performance obligation and the related warranty and repairs/maintenance costs are recorded as incurred.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-16</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000424_dcnt_6b7d37f8-896f-4591-8eec-db209476ae01" continuedAt="F_000424_dcnt_3d377147-6173-4c13-b130-a3aed6e80c3c"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000466" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Income taxes</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company estimates its income taxes separately for each tax jurisdiction in which it conducts operations. This process involves estimating actual current tax expense and assessing temporary differences resulting from the different treatment of items between book and tax which results in deferred tax assets and liabilities. The Company recognizes in income a change in tax rates on deferred tax assets and liabilities in the period that includes the enactment date. Valuation allowances are established when realization of deferred tax assets is not considered more likely than not. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company recognizes the effect of tax law changes in the period of enactment. Changes in existing tax laws and rates, their related interpretations, and the uncertainty generated by the current economic environment may affect the amounts of the Company&#8217;s deferred tax liabilities or the valuations of the Company&#8217;s deferred tax assets over time. The Company&#8217;s accounting for deferred tax consequences represents management&#8217;s best estimate of future events that can be appropriately reflected in the accounting estimates. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In determining whether the realization of deferred tax assets is considered to be more likely than not, the Company assesses the realizability of the deferred tax assets on a jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction basis. This assessment is dependent upon past operating results and projected profitability. The weight given to the positive and negative evidence is commensurate with the extent to which the evidence is objectively verified. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company accounts for uncertainty in income tax positions using a two-step approach. The first step is to determine whether it is more likely than not that a tax position will be sustained upon examination, including resolution of any related appeals or litigation processes, based on the technical merits of the position. The second step is to measure the tax position at the largest amount of benefit that is greater than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000602" name="orbc:PercentageOfAmountOfBenefits" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction>% likely of being realized upon ultimate settlement. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company recognizes interest and penalties related to uncertain tax positions in income tax expense. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000467" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loss contingencies </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company accrues for costs relating to litigation, claims and other contingent matters when such liabilities become probable and reasonably estimable. Such estimates may be based on advice from third parties or on management&#8217;s judgment, as appropriate. Actual amounts paid may differ from amounts estimated, and such differences will be charged to operations in the period in which the final determination of the liability is made. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000468" name="orbc:PreacquisitionContingenciesPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Pre-acquisition contingencies </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has evaluated pre-acquisition contingencies that existed as of the acquisition dates of the businesses acquired. If any pre-acquisition contingencies acquired as part of an acquisition become probable and estimable, the Company will record such amounts at fair market value in the measurement period, or the Company&#8217;s results of operations after the measurement period, as applicable. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000469" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stock-based compensation </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company measures and recognizes stock-based compensation expense for equity-based payment awards made to employees and directors based on estimated fair values on the date of grant. For equity-based payment awards, the Company recognizes compensation expense over the service period, net of estimated forfeitures using the straight-line method. For awards with non-market performance conditions, an evaluation is made at the grant date and future periods as to the likelihood of the performance criteria being met. Compensation expense is adjusted for changes in the likelihood of achieving the performance condition until the vesting date. For liability-based awards with market performance conditions, compensation expense is revalued at the end of each quarter based on the awards&#8217; fair value using the graded vesting attribution method over the vesting period. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000470" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000470_dcnt_1f75e0af-6450-4cdf-8421-42be201697c1">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recent accounting pronouncements </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU No. 2016-02 &#8220;Leases (Topic 842)&#8221; (&#8220;ASU 2016-02&#8221;), which is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2018. ASU 2016-02 requires an entity to recognize assets and liabilities arising from a lease for both finance and operating leases, along with additional qualitative and quantitative disclosures.&#160;The Company adopted ASU 2016-02 prospectively as of January 1, 2019, the date of initial application. As part of the adoption, the Company elected the package of practical expedients, the short-term lease exemption and the practical expedient to not separate lease and non-lease components. The Company completed its comprehensive review of its lease portfolio for all lease types and embedded leases throughout each region. Adoption of the new standard resulted in the recording of operating right-of-use assets and lease liabilities of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000603" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201602Member_20190101" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">10,892</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000604" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201602Member_20190101" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">13,825</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, as of January 1, 2019. Refer to &#8220;Note 15 &#8211; Leases&#8221; for more information.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-17</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000424_dcnt_3d377147-6173-4c13-b130-a3aed6e80c3c"><ix:continuation id="F_000470_dcnt_1f75e0af-6450-4cdf-8421-42be201697c1">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In January 2017, the FASB issued ASU No. 2017-04 &#8220;Intangibles &#8211; Goodwill and Other (Topic 350): Simplifying the Test for Goodwill Impairment&#8221; (&#8220;ASU 2017-04&#8221;)</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">,</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">which will be</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> effective for fiscal year</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">s</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">beginning after December 15, 2019</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. ASU 2017-04 removes Ste</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">p 2 of the goodwill impairment test, which requires a hypothetic</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">al purchase price allocation. Under ASU 2017-04</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">,</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> goodwill impairment will be the amount by which a reporting unit&#8217;s carrying value exceeds its fair value, not to exceed the carrying amount of goodwill. The adoption of this standard, which will be applied prospectively, is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June 2016, the FASB issued ASU No. 2016-13 &#8220;Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses (Topic 326): Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments&#8221; (&#8220;ASU 2016-13&#8221;), which will be effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2019. ASU 2016-13 introduces the current expected credit loss (CECL) model, which will require an entity to measure credit losses for certain financial instruments and financial assets. Upon initial recognition, an entity will be required to estimate a credit loss expected over the life of an exposure. The adoption of this standard is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</p></ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000425" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000425_dcnt_f96a07d2-e917-47bd-a767-52111e36d395">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note&#160;3.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Acquisitions </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2017 Business Development</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Blue Tree Systems Limited</p>

This method requires that assets acquired and liabilities assumed in a business combination be recognized at their fair values as of the acquisition date (the &#8220;Acquisition Method&#8221;). <p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-18</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000425_dcnt_f96a07d2-e917-47bd-a767-52111e36d395" continuedAt="F_000425_dcnt_780c48e8-07f2-4ea9-b958-681200446bc2">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Intangible Assets</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The estimated fair value of the technology and trademark intangible assets was determined using the &#8220;relief from royalty method&#8221; under the income approach, which is a valuation technique that provides an estimate of the fair value of an asset based on the costs savings that are available through ownership of the asset by the avoidance of paying royalties to license the use of the assets from another owner (the &#8220;Technology and Trademark Valuation Technique&#8221;). The estimated fair value of the customer lists was determined using the &#8220;excess earnings method&#8221; under the income approach, which represents the total income to be generated by the asset (the &#8220;Customer List Valuation Technique&#8221;). Some of the more significant assumptions inherent in the development of those asset valuations include the projected revenue associated with the asset, the appropriate discount rate to&#160;select in order to measure the risk inherent in each future cash flow stream, the assessment of each asset&#8217;s life cycle, as well as other factors. The discount rate used to arrive at the present value of the customer lists and technology at the acquisition date was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000629" name="orbc:DiscountRateToReflectRiskCharacteristics" contextRef="C_0001361983_srtConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_orbcORBCOMMTechnologyIrelandLimitedMember_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcBlueTreeSystemsLimitedMember_us-gaapFiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis_orbcCustomerListsTechnologyAndTrademarksMember_20171001_20171002" decimals="3" scale="-2">26.5</ix:nonFraction>%. The remaining useful lives of the technology and trademarks were based on historical product development cycles, the projected rate of technology migration and a market participant&#8217;s use of these intangible assets and the pattern of projected economic benefit of these intangible assets. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000476" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfFiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsAcquiredAsPartOfBusinessCombinationTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcBlueTreeSystemsLimitedMember_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000476_cnt_1">The remaining useful lives of customer lists were based on the customer attrition and the projected economic benefit of these customers.</ix:nonNumeric><span style="font-size:12pt;color:#000000;">&#160;</span></p><ix:continuation id="F_000476_cnt_1">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Blue Tree Acquisition solidified the Company&#8217;s transportation offering of fleet management and driver safety solutions to enterprises and industrial companies around the world that operate large commercial vehicle fleets. These factors contributed to a preliminary estimated purchase price resulting in the recognition of goodwill.&#160;The goodwill attributable to the Blue Tree Acquisition is not deductible for tax purposes.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Indemnification Asset</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the Share Purchase Agreement, the Company entered into an escrow agreement with the Sellers and an escrow agent. Under the terms of this escrow agreement,&#160;$<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000637" name="orbc:PurchasePriceCashConsiderationAmountDepositedInEscrow" contextRef="C_0001361983_srtConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_orbcORBCOMMTechnologyIrelandLimitedMember_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcBlueTreeSystemsLimitedMember_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_orbcIndemnificationAssetsMember_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">3,675</ix:nonFraction> was placed in an escrow account through April 2019 to fund any indemnification obligations to the Company under the Share Purchase Agreement. Under the terms of the escrow agreement, as of any release date for any portion of the escrow account amount, the value of any then submitted and unresolved indemnification claims will be retained in the escrow account until such time as the applicable claims are resolved.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Contingent Consideration</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Additional consideration was conditionally due to the Sellers upon achievement of certain financial milestones through December 2018. The fair value measurement of the contingent consideration obligation is determined using Level 3 unobservable inputs supported by little or no market activity based on the Company&#8217;s own assumptions. The estimated fair value of the contingent consideration was determined based on the Company&#8217;s preliminary estimates using the probability-weighted discounted cash flow approach. The financial milestone for this contingent consideration has not been met, and therefore, the Company recorded a reduction of the contingent liability of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000638" name="orbc:BusinessCombinationDecreaseContingentConsiderationEarnout" contextRef="C_0001361983_srtConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_orbcORBCOMMTechnologyIrelandLimitedMember_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcBlueTreeSystemsLimitedMember_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_us-gaapSellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpensesMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-3" scale="3">776</ix:nonFraction> in SG&#38;A expenses on the consolidated statement of operations for the year ended December 31, 2018.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Intangible Assets</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The estimated fair value of the technology intangible assets was determined using the &#8220;relief from royalty method&#8221; under the income approach, which is a valuation technique that provides an estimate of the fair value of an asset based on the costs savings that are available through ownership of the asset by the avoidance of paying royalties to license the use of the assets from another owner. The estimated fair value of the customer lists was determined using the Customer List Valuation Technique. Some of the more significant assumptions inherent in the development of those asset valuations include the projected revenue associated with the assets, the appropriate discount rate to&#160;select in order to measure the risk inherent in each future cash flow stream, the assessment of each asset&#8217;s life cycle, as well as other factors. The discount rate used to arrive at the acquisition date present value of the customer lists and technology was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000662" name="orbc:DiscountRateToReflectRiskCharacteristics" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_us-gaapFiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis_orbcCustomerListsAndTechnologyMember_20170608_20170609" decimals="2" scale="-2">12</ix:nonFraction>%. The remaining useful lives of the technology were based on historical product development cycles, the projected rate of technology migration and a market participant&#8217;s use of these intangible assets and the pattern of projected economic benefit of these intangible assets. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000478" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfFiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsAcquiredAsPartOfBusinessCombinationTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000478_cnt_1">The remaining useful lives of the customer lists were based on the customer attrition and projected economic benefit of these customers.</ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="F_000478_cnt_1">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Inthinc Acquisition allows the Company to offer fleet management and driver safety solutions to enterprises and industrial companies around the world that operate large commercial vehicle fleets. These factors contributed to a preliminary estimated purchase price resulting in the recognition of goodwill.&#160;The goodwill attributable to the Inthinc Acquisition is deductible for tax purposes.</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-20</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000425_dcnt_8aa350c9-dd5e-42a9-85c2-324217cb00d5">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Indemnification Asset</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the Asset Purchase Agreement, the Company entered into an escrow agreement with Inthinc and an escrow agent. Under the terms of this escrow agreement, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000669" name="orbc:PurchasePriceCashConsiderationAmountDepositedInEscrow" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_orbcIndemnificationAssetsMember_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">1,000</ix:nonFraction> was placed in an escrow account through September 9, 2019 to fund any working capital and indemnification obligations to the Company under the Asset Purchase Agreement. Under the terms of the escrow agreement, as of any release date for any portion of the escrow account amount, the value of any then submitted and unresolved indemnification claims would be retained in the escrow account until such time as the applicable claims are resolved. In the year ended December 31, 2018, the Company received $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000668" name="orbc:PurchasePriceCashConsiderationAmountReceivedFromEscrow" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_orbcIndemnificationAssetsMember_20190909" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">1,000</ix:nonFraction> from the escrow account to partially fund the working capital adjustment payment and indemnification obligations due to the Company and recorded a credit to SG&#38;A expenses. In addition, the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000670" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEquityInterestsIssuedOrIssuableNumberOfSharesIssued" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_orbcIndemnificationAssetsMember_20191001_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">76,796</ix:nonFraction> shares of ORBCOMM common stock issued as part of the purchase price for Inthinc have been cancelled by the Company in partial payment of the working capital adjustment due to the Company, and the Company recorded a credit in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000671" name="us-gaap:SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpense" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_orbcIndemnificationAssetsMember_20191001_20191231" decimals="-3" scale="3">526</ix:nonFraction> to SG&#38;A expenses in the quarter ended December 31, 2019 to reflect this cancellation.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Acquired Customer Product Obligation</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a result of the Inthinc Acquisition, the Company acquired customer product obligations on Inthinc&#8217;s product sales. The Company&#8217;s analysis of the customer product obligation is estimated based on Inthinc&#8217;s historical costs to replace or fix products for customers, as well as installation costs associated with these obligations. On June 9, 2017, the Company had estimated additional product obligations of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000672" name="us-gaap:ExtendedProductWarrantyAccrualAdditionsFromBusinessAcquisition" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_20170608_20170609" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">1,032</ix:nonFraction> relating to customer product obligations it was investigating associated with the Inthinc Acquisition as a result of undisclosed commitments made by Inthinc prior to the Company&#8217;s acquisition of Inthinc. As of December 31, 2019, the Company had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000673" name="us-gaap:AccruedLiabilitiesCurrent" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction> remaining liability on the consolidated balance sheet in connection with this acquired product liability obligation.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Contingent Consideration</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Additional consideration was conditionally due to the Inthinc sellers upon achievement of certain financial milestones through June 2019. The fair value measurement of the contingent consideration obligation was determined using Level 3 unobservable inputs supported by little or no market activity and based on the Company&#8217;s own assumptions. The estimated fair value of the contingent consideration was determined based on the Company&#8217;s estimates using the probability-weighted discounted cash flow approach.&#160;As of December 31, 2019 and 2018, the Company recorded $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000677" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationContingentConsiderationLiabilityCurrent" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_us-gaapAccruedLiabilitiesMember_20191231" decimals="-3" scale="3">0</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000678" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationContingentConsiderationLiabilityCurrent" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_us-gaapAccruedLiabilitiesMember_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">2,063</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, in accrued liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets in connection with the contingent consideration. All four financial milestones for this additional consideration were not met. Therefore, the Company recorded a reduction of the contingent liability of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000674" name="orbc:BusinessCombinationDecreaseContingentConsiderationEarnout" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_us-gaapSellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpensesMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">2,063</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000675" name="orbc:BusinessCombinationDecreaseContingentConsiderationEarnout" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_us-gaapSellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpensesMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">7,250</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000676" name="orbc:BusinessCombinationDecreaseContingentConsiderationEarnout" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcInthincTechnologySolutionsIncorporationMember_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_us-gaapSellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpensesMember_20170101_20171231" decimals="-3" scale="3">795</ix:nonFraction> in SG&#38;A expenses on the consolidated statements of operations for the years ended December&#160;31, 2019, 2018 and 2017, respectively. </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000426" name="us-gaap:DisclosureOfCompensationRelatedCostsShareBasedPaymentsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000426_dcnt_5e75297e-ea41-4dac-9c4a-72e030f2a7ac">

As of December&#160;31, 2019, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000791" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedShareBasedAwardsOtherThanOptions" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_orbcPerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">2,998</ix:nonFraction> of total unrecognized compensation cost related to these RSUs is expected to be recognized through March 2021. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair values of the time-based and performance-based RSU awards are based upon the closing stock price of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the date of grant. </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-23</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000426_dcnt_70e2559f-d2c6-4334-bacb-827a45052926">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Market </span><span style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Performance Units </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company grants Market Performance Units (&#8220;MPUs&#8221;) to its senior executives based on stock price performance over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000794">three-year</span> period measured on December&#160;31 of each year in the performance period. The MPUs will vest in equal installments at the end of each year in the performance period only if the Company satisfies the stock price performance targets and the senior executives <span style="color:#000000;">continue their employment through the dates the Compensation Committee has determined that the targets have been achieved.</span> The value of the MPUs that will be earned each year ranges up to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000792" name="orbc:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardMaximumPercentageOfEarningsOnEmployeeBaseSalaries" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_orbcMarketPerformanceUnitsMember_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">15</ix:nonFraction>% of each of the senior executive&#8217;s base salaries in the year of the grant depending on the Company&#8217;s stock price performance target for that year. The value of the MPUs can be paid in either cash, common stock or a combination of cash and common stock, at the Company&#8217;s discretion. The MPUs are classified as a liability on the consolidated balance sheets and are revalued at the end of each reporting period based on the awards&#8217; fair value over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000793">three-year</span> period. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2019, the Compensation Committee determined that the fiscal year 2019 stock price performance targets were not achieved for the 2019, 2018 and 2017 MPUs with respect to the 2019 performance year.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000485" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfShareBasedPaymentAwardEmployeeStockPurchasePlanValuationAssumptionsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_orbcMarketPerformanceUnitsMember_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As the MPUs contain both performance and service conditions, they have been treated as a series of three separate awards, or tranches, for purposes of recognizing stock-based compensation expense. The Company recognizes stock-based compensation expense on a tranche-by-tranche basis over the requisite service period for that specific tranche. The Company estimated the fair values of the MPUs using a Monte Carlo simulation model that used the following assumptions: </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000427" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerShareTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note&#160;5.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Net Income (Loss) Attributable to ORBCOMM Inc. Common Stockholders </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company accounts for earnings per share (&#8220;EPS&#8221;) in accordance with ASC Topic&#160;260 &#8220;Earnings Per Share&#8221; (&#8220;ASC 260&#8221;) and related guidance, which requires two calculations of EPS to be disclosed: basic and diluted. The numerator in calculating basic and diluted EPS is an amount equal to the net income (loss) attributable to ORBCOMM Inc. common stockholders for the periods presented. The denominator in calculating basic EPS is the weighted average shares outstanding for the respective periods. The denominator in calculating diluted EPS is the weighted average shares outstanding, plus the dilutive effect of stock option grants, unvested SAR and RSU grants and shares of Series A convertible preferred stock for the respective periods. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000486" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfEarningsPerShareBasicAndDilutedTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000486_cnt_1">The following table sets forth the basic and diluted EPS calculations for the years ended December&#160;31, 2019, 2018 and 2017:</ix:nonNumeric> </p><ix:continuation id="F_000486_cnt_1">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">One OG2 satellite that was launched in December 2015 experienced a solar array anomaly in July 2016 that resulted in the satellite entering a safe mode and being taken out of commercial service.&#160;<span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">This satellite had previously been intermittently providing AIS service and regularly communicating with the ground infrastructure.&#160;</span>In April 2017, communication was lost with this OG2 satellite.&#160;The Company&#8217;s satellite engineering team developed and uploaded new software designed to prevent a similar solar array anomaly from occurring on other OG2 satellites.&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June 2017, there was a loss of communication with the prototype OG2 satellite that was launched in December 2015, and in July 2017 there was&#160;a loss of communication with an OG2 satellite that was launched in July 2014. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000431" name="orbc:NotePayableRelatedPartyDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note&#160;9.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Note Payable &#8212; Related Party </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the acquisition of a majority interest in Satcom International Group plc in 2005, the Company recorded an indebtedness to OHB Technology A.G. (formerly known as OHB Teledata A.G.), a stockholder of the Company. At December&#160;31, 2019 and 2018, the principal balance of the note payable was &#8364;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217EUR" id="F_000982" name="orbc:PrincipalBalanceOfNotePayable" contextRef="C_0001361983_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217EUR" id="F_000983" name="orbc:PrincipalBalanceOfNotePayable" contextRef="C_0001361983_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">1,138</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>, with a carrying value of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000984" name="us-gaap:NotesPayableRelatedPartiesNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001361983_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">1,275</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000985" name="us-gaap:NotesPayableRelatedPartiesNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001361983_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">1,298</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. The carrying value was based on the note&#8217;s estimated fair value at the time of acquisition. The difference between the carrying value and principal balance was being amortized to interest expense over the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000986">six-year</span> estimated life, which ended on September&#160;30, 2011. This note does not bear interest and has no fixed repayment term. Repayment of the note will be made from the distribution profits (as defined in the note agreement) of ORBCOMM Europe LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company. The note has been classified as long-term, as the Company does not expect any repayments to be required prior to December 31, 2020. </p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Senior Secured Notes</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On April 10, 2017, the Company issued $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000987" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_orbcEightPercentSeniorSecuredNotesDueTwoThousandAndTwentyFourMember_20170410" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">250,000</ix:nonFraction> aggregate principal amount of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000988" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_orbcEightPercentSeniorSecuredNotesDueTwoThousandAndTwentyFourMember_20170410" decimals="INF" scale="-2">8.0</ix:nonFraction>% senior secured notes due <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000989" name="orbc:DebtInstrumentMaturityYear" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_orbcEightPercentSeniorSecuredNotesDueTwoThousandAndTwentyFourMember_20170410_20170410">2024</ix:nonNumeric> (the &#8220;Senior Secured Notes&#8221;). Such limitations have various baskets as set forth in the </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Revolving </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Credit Agreement.</span></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-32</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000435_dcnt_72b1298f-758b-4d70-90e5-4a84b73d0dcd" continuedAt="F_000435_dcnt_88b99af6-83bd-411c-aa89-aed38fcec4d0">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December 22, 2017, new federal tax reform legislation was enacted in the United States, resulting in significant changes from previous tax law. The <span style="color:#000000;">U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (the &#8220;2017 Tax Act&#8221;)</span> reduced the federal corporate income tax rate to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001194" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">21</ix:nonFraction>% from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001193" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001361983_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20170101_20171231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">35</ix:nonFraction>% effective January 1, 2018. The 2017 Tax Act also changes the taxation of foreign earnings, and companies generally will not be subject to United States federal income taxes upon the receipt of dividends from foreign subsidiaries and will not be permitted foreign tax credits related to such dividends. Additionally, upon enactment, there is a one-time deemed repatriation tax on undistributed foreign earnings and profits (the &#8220;transition tax&#8221;).&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The key impacts of the 2017 Tax Act on the Company&#8217;s financial statements were the re-measurement of deferred tax balances to the new corporate tax rate and the calculation of any impacts of the transition tax. The re-measurement of the deferred tax balances to the new corporate rate is complete and those amounts are not provisional. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Although the Company has taxable earnings and profits from its foreign subsidiaries, the Company had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001195" name="orbc:CashTaxPaymentsForTransitionTax" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction> cash tax payments for the transition tax. The amount of taxable foreign earnings and profits was significantly less than the Company&#8217;s expected tax losses for 2017, therefore, the Company utilized these losses to offset the income inclusion regarding the transition tax. The Company has determined that it will elect an accounting policy to treat tax on global intangible low-taxed income inclusions under the 2017 Tax Act as a period cost when incurred.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As part of the Company&#8217;s accounting for the acquisitions, a portion of the purchase price was allocated to goodwill. The acquired goodwill is deductible for tax purposes and amortized over <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001196" name="us-gaap:FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetUsefulLife" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapFiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis_us-gaapGoodwillMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">fifteen years</ix:nonNumeric> for income tax purposes. Under GAAP, the acquired goodwill is not amortized in the Company&#8217;s financial statements. As such, a deferred income tax expense and a deferred tax liability arise as a result of the tax deductibility for this amount for tax purposes but not for financial statement purposes. The resulting deferred tax liability, which is expected to continue to increase over time, will remain on the Company&#8217;s balance sheet indefinitely unless there is an impairment of the asset. As a result of the 2017 Tax Act and the changes it made to net operating loss carryforward rules, the Company is now able to use the above deferred tax liability as a source of future taxable income in evaluating the need for a valuation allowance. This change resulted in a deferred tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001197" name="us-gaap:TaxCutsAndJobsActOf2017IncompleteAccountingChangeInTaxRateDeferredTaxLiabilityProvisionalIncomeTaxBenefit" contextRef="C_0001361983_20170101_20171231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">1,693</ix:nonFraction> during the year ended December 31, 2017.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2019 and 2018, the Company maintained a valuation allowance against all of its net deferred tax assets, excluding goodwill, attributable to operations in the United States as the realization was not considered more likely than not. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The net change in the total valuation allowance for the years ended December&#160;31, 2019, 2018 and 2017 was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001198" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowancesAndReservesPeriodIncreaseDecrease" contextRef="C_0001361983_20190101_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">2,499</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001199" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowancesAndReservesPeriodIncreaseDecrease" contextRef="C_0001361983_20180101_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">6,124</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001200" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowancesAndReservesPeriodIncreaseDecrease" contextRef="C_0001361983_20170101_20171231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">6,458</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 1, 2017, the Company adopted ASU No. 2016-09 &#8220;Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting.&#8221; Prior to adopting the ASU, the Company recognized tax benefits associated with the exercise of SARs and stock options and vesting of RSUs directly to stockholders&#8217; equity only when the tax benefit reduces income tax payable on the basis that a cash tax&#160;savings has occurred. As a result of adopting this ASU the Company recognized the benefit of net operating loss carryforwards that were created as a result of previous windfall tax deductions. The gross amount of windfall deductions that were previously not recognized was approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001201" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationTaxBenefitFromCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201609Member_20161230_20170102" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">6,529</ix:nonFraction>. Due to a full valuation allowance, the recognition of the benefit for the windfall deductions did not have any impact to the consolidated balance sheet or consolidated statement of operations for the years ended December 31, 2019 and 2018. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2019 and 2018, the Company had potentially utilizable federal net operating loss carryforwards of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001202" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">125,870</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001203" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">108,746</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. As of December 31, 2019 and 2018, the Company had potentially utilizable state net operating loss carryforwards of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001204" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapStateAndLocalJurisdictionMember_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">159,083</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001205" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapStateAndLocalJurisdictionMember_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">232,256</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. The federal net operating loss carryforwards expire at various times through <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001206" name="orbc:DomesticOperatingLossCarryForwardsExpirationYear" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20190101_20191231">2037</ix:nonNumeric> for losses incurred prior to January 1, 2018. All federal net operating losses incurred after January 1, 2018 have an indefinite life. The state net operating loss carryforwards expire at various times through <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001207" name="orbc:DomesticOperatingLossCarryForwardsExpirationYear" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapStateAndLocalJurisdictionMember_20190101_20191231">2039</ix:nonNumeric> for states that do not follow the federal rule having an indefinite life for losses incurred after 2018. As of December&#160;31, 2019 and 2018, the Company had potentially utilizable foreign net operating loss carryforwards of <span>$<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001208" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapForeignCountryMember_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">14,035</ix:nonFraction><span style="font-size:12pt;">&#160;</span></span>and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001209" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapForeignCountryMember_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">15,989</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. The foreign net operating loss carryforwards expire on various dates through <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001210" name="orbc:DomesticOperatingLossCarryForwardsExpirationYear" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapForeignCountryMember_20190101_20191231">2039</ix:nonNumeric>. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The utilization of the Company&#8217;s net operating losses may be subject to a substantial limitation due to the &#8220;change of ownership provisions&#8221; under Section&#160;382 of the Internal Revenue Code and similar state provisions. Such limitation may result in the expiration of the net operating loss carryforwards before their utilization. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2019, the Company has not provided deferred income taxes on the undistributed earnings of its foreign subsidiaries. The amount of such earnings was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001211" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxLiabilitiesUndistributedForeignEarnings" contextRef="C_0001361983_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_orbcForeignSubsidiariesMember_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">21,677</ix:nonFraction>. These earnings have been permanently reinvested and the Company does not plan to initiate action that would precipitate the payment of income taxes thereon. It is not practicable to estimate the amount of additional tax that might be payable on these undistributed earnings.</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-33</p>
